ruleSet.name: industry-sop-gap-closure
ruleSet.description: Rules closing genuine gaps against standard telecom NOC / ITIL industry SOPs, identified by auditing the existing rule base (all 6 merged packs) rather than assumed. Three of the four action fields used here (escalateVendor, regulatoryReportingRequired, regulatoryReportingDeadlineHours) were already declared in the original 35-rule base pack's vocabulary but never actually triggered by any rule -- these rules fill that in. See docs/industry-sop-gap-closure.md for the full audit.

rules.name: Vendor-Attributed Root Cause Escalation (Underpinning Contract)
rules.description: Root cause has been attributed to a vendor-supplied component covered by an Underpinning Contract (UPC); standard vendor-management SOP is to escalate through the vendor's contractual support channel with its own response-time clock, rather than routing to internal engineering alone. The action field this writes, escalateVendor, was already declared in the base rule pack's vocabulary but no rule ever set it.

rules.name: Change Freeze Violation
rules.description: A change linked to this incident was made during a declared change-freeze window (e.g. holiday freeze, peak-event blackout) without emergency-change approval -- a change-freeze policy violation under standard ITIL/CAB governance, distinct from the existing unapproved-maintenance rules (which fire on changeApproved==false; a freeze violation can occur even with normal approval, since a freeze requires additional emergency sign-off beyond the standard approval process). Requires Change Advisory Board review; priority is floored at High regardless of technical severity, since the freeze violation itself is an operational governance failure worth surfacing on its own.

rules.name: Mass Regional Outage -- Regulatory Reporting Threshold
rules.description: Estimated user-minutes of impact (affected users x outage duration) crosses the mass-outage regulatory reporting threshold used by major telecom regulators (e.g. FCC NORS-style 900,000 user-minutes, and comparable Ofcom/TRAI thresholds), independent of whether emergency services are affected. R008/R020 already cover the emergency-services-line trigger for regulatoryReportingRequired; this closes the separate, broader mass-outage-scale trigger the base pack's own vocabulary anticipated (regulatoryReportingDeadlineHours already exists as a field, used here for the standard 24-hour reporting window) but never populated for this case. Formal regulatory reporting is required; priority is nudged up one level (not force-set), consistent with how R013/R016-style modifiers already behave.
